title.narrative: Fragmentation Of Peacemaking And Peacebuilding: Non-Western Dynamics Of Peace And Transition Management

description.narrative: The objective of this programme of work is to capture the impact of two broader geopolitical trends on trajectories of peacemaking and peacebuilding practices and norms: (1) the rise of potential global rivals to Western approaches; and (2) the rise of regional approaches as an alternative to global ones, with a focus on the Middle East and Africa. The goal is to map the fragmentation of peacemaking and peacebuilding approaches and to assess to what extent non-Western approaches work in complementarity with Western statebuilding efforts, and to what extent they present a competing vision of peacemaking and peacebuilding that is in competition with more normative approaches to statebuilding. We aim to examine not just the alternative practices, but also provide an appraisal of whether and how these practices challenge the normative order developed in the aftermath of the Cold War, and underpinning peacebuilding practice since then. This mapping is a Phase One baseline study, across a range of case studies and domains, which could be built on if findings and funds permitted.
